meta.note: Dining options are NOT included in holiday package budgets. They are shown as nearby suggestions only. Price bands: $ = quick/affordable ($8-18pp), $$ = casual family dining ($18-35pp), $$$ = premium ($35-60+pp). Opening hours may vary — check before visiting.

venues.name: Betty's Burgers & Concrete Co
venues.notes: Cult burger chain in the CBD — smashed patties, loaded fries, and famous concrete frozen custard desserts. Fast, casual, consistent. Kids love the custard.

venues.name: Guzman y Gomez South Bank
venues.notes: Fast, fresh Mexican right on Grey Street. Burrito bowls, nachos, kids' menu. Quick lunch between museums or parklands.

venues.name: Max Brenner Chocolate Bar
venues.notes: The bald man makes chocolate — famous for chocolate pizza, fondue, hot chocolate, and decadent desserts. Kids go absolutely wild here. A holiday treat.

venues.name: Vici Dining
venues.notes: Authentic Italian at South Bank — handmade pasta, wood-fired pizza, excellent antipasti. Family-friendly, generous portions. Bottomless pasta Wednesdays for $40.

venues.name: Riverbar & Kitchen
venues.notes: Waterfront dining on the Eagle Street Pier — burgers, seafood, share plates. Incredible river and Story Bridge views. Kids' menu available.

venues.name: Felix for Good Fortune
venues.notes: Brisbane's most loved cafe — legendary breakfasts, big portions, excellent coffee. The smashed avo is famous. Queue at weekends but worth it.

venues.name: Alfred & Constance
venues.notes: Eclectic venue across three heritage buildings — pub grub, cocktails, outdoor courtyard. Kids welcome in the main pub area. Fortitude Valley institution.

venues.name: Hellenika at The Calile
venues.notes: Brisbane's best Greek restaurant — poolside at The Calile, authentic dishes, incredible atmosphere. Special occasion dining in James Street precinct.

venues.name: Gordita
venues.notes: Tiny hole-in-the-wall taqueria in Fortitude Valley — authentic tacos, fresh salsas, amazing value. Stand-up eating, but worth it for the flavours.

venues.name: The Bird
venues.notes: Laid-back rooftop bar and restaurant in the CBD — burgers, tacos, cocktails. Family-acceptable earlier in the evening, great city views.

venues.name: Strangers in Paradise Cafe
venues.notes: Brisbane's best rooftop brunch spot — colourful pancakes, smoothie bowls, epic coffee. Relaxed vibe, excellent for a weekend breakfast.

venues.name: The Bavarian
venues.notes: German beer and food hall at Eagle Street — massive pretzels, schnitzels, sausages, share platters. Lively, loud, very kid-friendly at early sittings.

venues.name: Midtown Centre Cafe
venues.notes: Underground laneway cafe in the CBD — excellent coffee, bagels, sandwiches. A hidden local gem for a quick breakfast.

venues.name: La Cucina South Bank
venues.notes: Classic Italian trattoria on Little Stanley Street — wood-fired pizzas, handmade pasta, generous serves. Outdoor seating watching South Bank pass by. Very family-friendly.

venues.name: Luke's Kitchen
venues.notes: CBD restaurant from a MasterChef contestant — beautifully presented dishes, excellent service. Lunch is a better value proposition for families.

venues.name: Wild Things Are Cafe
venues.notes: Cute cafe serving colourful toasties, fresh juices, and excellent coffee in a bright, airy space. Family-friendly seating.

venues.name: Eat Street Northshore
venues.notes: 70+ food vendors from around the world at Hamilton — dumplings, bao, tacos, crepes, loaded fries, gelato. $3 entry (adults), kids free. Best family night out in Brisbane.

venues.name: Domino's Pizza (various)
venues.notes: Cheap pizza for the night you can't be bothered. $5 value pizzas, delivery or pickup. Dozens of locations across Brisbane.
